title: Species compositions of egg parasitoids of the genus Trissolcus and their host fruit-piercing stink bugs collected by sweeping methods in Japan
content:
Abstract
The brown marmorated stink bug, Halyomorpha halys (Stål) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae), is native to East Asia and has invaded North America and Europe. In the present study, surveys of egg parasitoids of the genus Trissolcus and 3 fruit-piercing stink bugs: H. halys, Plautia stali Scott (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae), and Glaucias subpunctatus (Walker) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae), were conducted with sweep nets from 2018 to 2020 in Japan to clarify their species compositions. This method is independent of the type and condition of egg masses unlike the sentinel egg mass exposure method. Therefore, it is possible to capture the adult egg parasitoid assemblage associated with host habitats. Although a diverse composition of fruit-piercing stink bugs was observed depending on the sampling site, Trissolcus japonicus (Ashmead) (Hymenoptera: Scelionidae) was the dominant species in most areas. These areas contained a low percentage of H. halys and a high percentage of P. stali or G. subpunctatus. Trissolcus japonicus is considered the most important natural enemy of H. halys in its native region, as inferred from its preference results. However, it has often been observed that T. japonicus emerges from eggs of P. stali and G. subpunctatus in Japan, and the frequent collection of T. japonicus in habitats dominated by these stink bugs in this study is consistent with a relatively broad host range in the field. Therefore, further research is needed on the comprehensive relationship between T. japonicus and the available stink bug species, including H. halys, that can serve as hosts in their native regions.
